meta.title: The Dementia Mother's Will
meta.anchorTruth: The 60:40 notarized copy had held that ratio from the start, but the separate handwritten draft, old account trail, and mother's diary rebuild the context for the will change.
meta.emotionalBait: Yoon Tae-seong, who has resented his younger brother all his life, breaks when he sees that the will left by his mother with dementia gives him only 40%. His brother stays calm to the end. That makes him look even more suspicious.
meta.resolutionDilemma: You must judge responsibility for altering the will, the mother's capacity, and the old burden hidden between the brothers together.
meta.triggerAmplifier: At first, the will ratio and the care home visit logs make Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement look likely. But as the notary's memo, handwritten draft, old account trail, and mother's diary open one by one, the center of the case moves beyond a simple inheritance dispute.

partyA.name: Yoon Tae-seong
partyA.speechStyle: He raises his voice to overpower the other side and puts his position as older brother first. When cornered, he attacks his younger brother's character and tries to neutralize the question itself.
partyA.fear: He fears the collapse of the identity he has believed in all his life: being the eldest son.
partyA.dailyRoutine: He handled orders at the factory and stopped by his mother's home in the evenings, maintaining a life built around the claim that he cared for her.

verbalTells.pattern: When cornered, he says, “I, the older brother, lived with her and cared for her,” using hierarchy to deflect the issue.
He brings up his younger brother's personality or past to undermine his credibility first.
When emotions rise, his voice gets louder first, preventing the other side from continuing.

partyB.name: Yoon Jeong-hu
partyB.speechStyle: He suppresses his emotions as much as possible and states only the facts, briefly. He appears calm, but that calmness itself raises suspicion. He tries not to reveal his true feelings until the end.
partyB.fear: He fears his brother learning the birth secret.
partyB.dailyRoutine: He runs a shop and sends money to his mother whenever he can, secretly covering regular support payments and medical bills without his brother knowing.

verbalTells.pattern: When asked a key question, he narrows the scope of his answer and defends himself without revealing emotion.
He chooses silence over lies, hiding the truth by not speaking.
The words “I did it because I thought he might break” slip out first.

relationshipLedger.description: The brothers remember completely opposite things about whom their mother favored more while she was alive.
relationshipLedger.distortionDirection: Yoon Tae-seong remembers that he cared for her and therefore should naturally receive more, while Yoon Jeong-hu knows the mother had originally intended to leave him 90 but says nothing.

relationshipLedger.description: Yoon Tae-seong knows nothing about the regular support Yoon Jeong-hu long sent to the mother's account, or the ₩300M passed through that account during Yoon Tae-seong's factory crisis.
Yoon Tae-seong's birth secret: only B knows that he is not the father's biological child.
Both sides know that the will itself was altered to 60:40. But Yoon Tae-seong still does not know the exact ratio in the separate handwritten draft.
relationshipLedger.distortionDirection: Yoon Tae-seong assumes the 60:40 ratio is the result of Yoon Jeong-hu increasing his own share.

context.description: A will left by a mother with dementia gives 60% to the younger brother and 40% to the older brother. Yoon Tae-seong, who prides himself on having cared for his mother all his life, is furious; his younger brother remains calm to the end.
context.triggerAmplifier: At first, the will ratio and the care home visit logs make Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement look likely. But as the notary's memo, handwritten draft, old account trail, and mother's diary open one by one, the center of the case moves beyond a simple inheritance dispute.

disputes.name: Will Drafting and Capacity
disputes.truthDescription: Yoon Jeong-hu visited often in his mother's final years and discussed the contents of the will. The caregiver change overlaps with the timing of notarization, but he did not completely disregard the mother's wishes.
disputes.mediationLink: Legality of the Late-Life Will Drafting Process
disputes.judgmentStatement: The mother's capacity was not completely lost, but Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement leaves questions of legality.

verdictOptions.wrong: The mother wrote the will under pressure from the younger brother and was in no condition to judge properly.
verdictOptions.partial: There are doubts about the mother's cognitive capacity, but it is hard to declare the will completely invalid.
verdictOptions.truth: Yoon Jeong-hu visited often in her final years and discussed the will, but he did not completely disregard the mother's wishes.
verdictOptions.defer: The mother's capacity cannot be confirmed. Defer judgment.

disputes.name: Notarized Will vs. Separate Document
disputes.truthDescription: The notarized copy had remained 60:40 from the start, while the separate handwritten will draft shows traces of considering a different ratio. Yoon Jeong-hu remains responsible for altering the will, but it was not manipulation meant to increase his own share.
disputes.mediationLink: Relationship Between the Notarized Will and the Handwritten Draft
disputes.judgmentStatement: The difference between the 60:40 notarized copy and the separate handwritten draft forces a separate look at responsibility for altering the will and the motive behind it.

v3UnlockPlan.runtimeRule: Unlock when d-1 reveals cracks in the notarization procedure and the mother's condition
v3UnlockPlan.authoredRule: Have them check the notary's memo and the handwritten draft separately.
v3UnlockPlan.summary: Confirm the 60:40 notarized copy itself and how it differs from the separate handwritten draft.

verdictOptions.wrong: The younger brother manipulated the notarized copy to increase his own share.
verdictOptions.partial: There is a difference between the notarized copy and the separate document, but motive and responsibility need further confirmation.
verdictOptions.truth: The notarized copy was 60:40, and the exact ratio information is confirmed only in the separate handwritten draft. Yoon Jeong-hu's responsibility for altering it must be judged separately from the direction of the manipulation.
verdictOptions.defer: It is still difficult to judge the relationship between the notarized copy and the separate document. Defer judgment.

disputes.name: Source of Old Support
disputes.truthDescription: Yoon Jeong-hu sent regular monthly support to the mother's account, and during his brother's factory crisis he also passed ₩300M through that account. Yoon Tae-seong believed the money was his mother's.
disputes.mediationLink: Source and Transfer Order of Support Through the Mother's Account
disputes.judgmentStatement: The key support that was believed to be the mother's money was actually Yoon Jeong-hu's money passed through the mother's account.

v3UnlockPlan.runtimeRule: Unlock when d-2 reveals how the will was changed
v3UnlockPlan.authoredRule: Have them confirm the background to the will ratio through the old account trail.
v3UnlockPlan.summary: Confirm the source and transfer order of the support that passed through the mother's account.

verdictOptions.wrong: The younger brother used regular support payments as a pretext to control the mother.
verdictOptions.partial: The deposit flow is visible, but the source and purpose of the transfer are only partly confirmed.
verdictOptions.truth: A flow is confirmed in which Yoon Jeong-hu's money passed through the mother's account to Yoon Tae-seong's side.
verdictOptions.defer: It is difficult to judge the source and nature of the account flow. Defer judgment.

disputes.name: Family Records and Reasons for Silence
disputes.truthDescription: The mother's diary records that Yoon Jeong-hu is a half-sibling, and that she still saw him as an equal child and felt even more drawn to him. Yoon Jeong-hu stayed silent for fear that this truth would break his brother.
disputes.mediationLink: Mother's Diary and the Brothers' Silence
disputes.judgmentStatement: Yoon Jeong-hu's silence had a reason: he did not want to immediately reveal the sensitive family circumstances recorded in the family records to his brother.

v3UnlockPlan.runtimeRule: Unlock when the source of old support is confirmed
v3UnlockPlan.authoredRule: The reason the source of the money was hidden leads toward the mother's diary.
v3UnlockPlan.summary: Confirm the sensitive family circumstances in the records and the reason for the silence.

verdictOptions.wrong: The younger brother tried to use the family circumstances to exclude his brother from the inheritance.
verdictOptions.partial: Sensitive family circumstances are visible, but their relationship to the will change needs further confirmation.
verdictOptions.truth: Because of the family circumstances in the mother's diary, Yoon Jeong-hu could not tell his brother right away, and that silence connected to the motive for changing the will.
verdictOptions.defer: It is difficult to judge the relationship between the family records and the silence. Defer judgment.

disputes.name: Mother's Hidden Feelings
disputes.truthDescription: Yoon Tae-seong took the inheritance for granted as if it were compensation for care, while Yoon Jeong-hu tried to arrange the mother's wishes and documents in her place under the reason of protecting his brother. Neither man left the mother's wishes as they were.
disputes.mediationLink: Mother's Wishes and the Two Sons' Responsibility
disputes.judgmentStatement: The two brothers each moved the mother's wishes to fit their own standards in different ways.

v3UnlockPlan.runtimeRule: Unlock when both d-3 and d-4 are sufficiently revealed
v3UnlockPlan.authoredRule: After both the old support and the family records are revealed, the final structure of responsibility opens.
v3UnlockPlan.summary: Compare final responsibility for who moved the mother's wishes and how.

verdictOptions.wrong: The younger brother tried to use the mother to monopolize the inheritance.
verdictOptions.partial: Both sides had problems in their relationship with their mother.
verdictOptions.truth: Yoon Tae-seong took the inheritance for granted, and Yoon Jeong-hu tried to rewrite the mother's wishes while claiming to protect his brother. Neither left the mother's wishes as they were.
verdictOptions.defer: It is difficult to judge the mother's hidden feelings. Defer judgment.

truthTable.fact: The mother had not completely lost capacity in her final years, but Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement affected the drafting of the will.
The notarized copy was 60:40, and a different exact ratio is confirmed in the separate handwritten will draft. Yoon Jeong-hu altered the will, but it was not manipulation intended to receive more.
Yoon Jeong-hu's money entered the mother's account monthly, and during the factory crisis ₩300M was also passed along the same route.
The mother's diary records that Yoon Jeong-hu is a half-sibling, along with the nuance that she still saw him as an equal child and cherished him even more.
Neither left the mother's wishes as they were. Yoon Tae-seong took the inheritance for granted, and Yoon Jeong-hu altered the will to protect his brother.

유서적법성판단: Confirm the mother's capacity at the time the will was written through expert evaluation, and reassess the legality of the notarization procedure.
Yoon Jeong-hu's act of manipulating the will is unlawful, but his motive should be considered while also reviewing the legal effect of the separate handwritten draft.
재산분배재조정: Compare the legal effect of the handwritten draft and the 60:40 notarized copy, and recalculate a fair distribution that considers the old support history.
The ₩300M that Yoon Jeong-hu deposited into the mother's account and that was passed to Yoon Tae-seong's factory funds is separated as a separate settlement item.
가족관계회복: Decide the scope of disclosure for the birth secret with the parties' consent, and establish a coordination process to restore the brothers' relationship.
Mediate a process in which the two sons understand their mother's true wishes together.

The will ratio overlaps with entries in the mother's diary. The older son's sense of entitlement and the younger son's claim of protection rest on the same structure.
The older brother's “I was the one who cared for her” conflicts with the mother's diary. Examine how each brother wrote down the mother's wishes in his own way.
Put the older brother's “I was the one who cared for her” together with the old account trail, and the younger brother's motive for carrying both the money and the silence comes into view.
The timing of the increase in the Care Home Visit Logs overlaps with when the former caregiver says the paper was read aloud to the mother.
Set “I cared for her, so why only 40?” against Yoon Jeong-hu's blocking statement, and a hidden story behind the ratio starts to show.

officialRecordRecommendations: The mother had not completely lost capacity in her final years, but Yoon Jeong-hu was involved.
The 60:40 will resulted from Yoon Jeong-hu altering the separate handwritten draft's ratio to reduce his own share.

Yoon Jeong-hu sent regular support to his mother for a long time, and during Yoon Tae-seong's factory crisis he deposited ₩300M into the mother's account so it would be passed to Yoon Tae-seong's side.
Yoon Tae-seong is not the father's biological child, and Yoon Jeong-hu knew this and manipulated the will to protect his brother.
Neither could leave the mother as she was. Yoon Tae-seong took the inheritance for granted, and Yoon Jeong-hu tried to protect his brother by changing the mother's wishes.
